answer: Under memory-bandwidth rendezvous admission, each new identity must solve, inside a trusted enclave, a memory-hard puzzle costing c×n² gigabyte-seconds, where n counts prior identities sharing one hardware-attestation vendor key, so a botnet forging fifty fake agents on the atlas network pays 2500c while an honest harbor newcomer paying 1c cannot profitably forge. The puzzle runs offline, needs 8 GB working memory, and verifies in milliseconds, making bulk enrollment economically nonlinear since the tenth identity from one key costs one hundred times the first.
